answer.summary: Lean into your strengths, but stay aware of your weaknesses: teammates can complement them, while unrecognized weaknesses create friction and slow the team down. You do not need to fix every weakness; know who can cover it.

sections.heading: The tradeoff
sections.content: LaPointe supports leaning into strengths, but warns against doing so to the point of ignoring weaknesses. On a team, another person’s strength can patch your weakness; if you are unaware of that weakness, it can flare up and make others translate things into your preferred language, slowing everyone down. A team that is unaware of its weaknesses tends to experience slowness and problems.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.content: You do not have to fix every weakness. Be aware of where you are weak and know which teammate can complement or patch that gap. LaPointe describes the team’s strengths as varying with the situation, so people can contribute differently as needs change.
